name: Hands
example: “Test the Notes app for me” — an AI agent uses your apps, with your permission.
prompt.title: A program running on your account asked to control your computer
prompt.what: It could see your windows, take screenshots, click, scroll and type in your apps until you stop it.
prompt.name: It calls itself: {client}
prompt.reported: The name and the program are reported by the program, not verified. Allow it only if you just started it yourself.
prompt.never: It can never use password fields, permission or password prompts, the lock screen or Settings → AI → Hands.
settings.toggle: Let an AI agent use this computer
settings.what: Claude Code or Lumo can read your windows, click, type and take screenshots, the way you would. Each program asks you first.
settings.session: This switch is for this session only: when you log out it turns off again.
settings.can1: List your windows and read what they show: buttons, fields, menus and lists.
settings.can2: Click, scroll, drag, type and press keys, through the same path as your own mouse and keyboard.
settings.can3: Take screenshots of a window or a display, open apps and files, and read an app's log.
settings.can4: Pause by itself for a few seconds whenever you move the mouse or type.
settings.never1: Read or type into password fields, or read a password.
settings.never2: See or answer permission, password, keyring or administrator prompts, the lock screen or the login screen.
settings.never3: See or change this page, so it can't turn itself on or widen its own list of apps.
settings.never4: Run commands: LordOS gives it no way to.
settings.stop: While an agent is working, a banner on every display says so. Stop in the banner, or Ctrl+Alt+Esc on your keyboard, stops every agent at once.
settings.allowAll: No app chosen: the agent may use every app.

settings.allowSome.one: The agent may use only the {count} app chosen.
settings.allowSome.other: The agent may use only the {count} apps chosen.

settings.how: Run this once in a terminal. Claude Code then has LordOS's tools; the first time it connects, LordOS asks you.
settings.qa: To test an app without touching your desktop, Claude Code can use “lordos-mcp --headless notes”: a private desktop with sample files that nobody sees.
